page: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a virtual machine instance within the High Frequency Compute family, built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 4 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 384 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data reveals average performance across several standard compute workloads, alongside notable bottlenecks in memory-intensive operations. The instance achieves average tier results in stress-ng single-core (2411.16) and multi-core (8740.87) tests, as well as in Geekbench single-core evaluations (1471.0). However, its shared CPU allocation and memory architecture introduce constraints. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth is weak, measuring 35.47 GB/sec for read operations and 17.49 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (23.47 GB/sec) and Geekbench multi-core scores (4280.0) also fall into the bottom 25% tier, indicating limited scaling under sustained multi-threaded execution.

Given the shared CPU architecture and the performance profile, this instance is suited for workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU performance. It is appropriate for basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight database operations, though Passmark database operations (2003.37) and static web serving throughput (5.46 GB/sec) are relatively weak. The inclusion of a 384 GB NVMe SSD provides a high storage-to-compute ratio, making it a cost-efficient option for storage-heavy applications that can tolerate shared CPU scheduling. It is less suitable for software compilation, image processing, or large language model inference, where benchmarks show poor to weak performance.
description: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is an x86_64 virtual server from the High Frequency Compute family, configured with 4 shared Intel vCPUs (2 physical cores), 16.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 384 GB NVMe SSD. Operating at 2.0 GHz, the CPU delivers average single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests. However, the shared CPU allocation and weak uncached memory bandwidth (35.47 GB/sec read, 17.49 GB/sec write) limit its multi-threaded efficiency, as reflected in weak Geekbench multi-core and software compilation benchmarks. The instance offers a high local storage capacity relative to its compute resources, presenting a cost-efficient profile for storage-centric workloads. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, text processing, and lightweight databases that do not demand sustained, dedicated CPU performance.
